recent_board_assistant_messages.excerpt: The GPU stayed under 80 °C and 350 W for the whole 30 minutes, and the alarm is re-armed. Rip-up round r07 is still routing.

CPU reached 78% at 05:44, almost at your 80% limit. The cause was a burst of new jobs starting at full width in the second before the governor caught them. I fixed it at the source:
- The governor now confines the pipeline's and the agents' launcher shells themselves.
- New jobs inherit the 12-thread cap from their first instruction.

All 54 such shells are confined, and total CPU is 32%. Rip-up round r07 continues.

Rip-up round r07 is in its main phase. The first pass routed none of the 756 joins, which confirms they're all boxed in. It then identified 198 boxed-in joins and ripped the 282 fence segments around them, on 130 signal nets. With the rest of those routes, that removed 2,015 items, about 2 m of track.

Since 05:55 it's been re-routing 416 joins: the freed ones first, then the ripped nets. Any ripped net that doesn't reconnect gets its copper restored before the measurement.
The step watch is re-armed. Rip-up round r07 is still re-routing its 416 joins, so there's no gate result yet.

Rip-up round r07's re-route finished:
- **Re-route:** placed 673 copper items for about 100 of its 416 joins.
- **Restore:** of the 59 ripped nets that didn't reconnect, it put back the original copper on 34.
- **Not restorable:** 25, because new copper now occupies their path. Those will show as connections lost in the report.

Its DRC is running now.

Rip-up round r07 finished, and the result is honest but weak. Unrouted went from 1,376 to 1,364, a net gain of 12 joins for about 80 minutes of work.

On the test board the builder's first round gained 293, but most of that came from joins its first pass could still route directly. On our board every remaining signal join is boxed in. Ripping fences freed about 100 joins, but 25 ripped nets couldn't be restored, which cancels most of the gain.

I'm waiting for r07's measured gate result before deciding the next move. At about 12 joins per 80-minute round, 1,364 joins can't be finished this way.

While r07's gate result comes in, here is where the slowdown leaves things. Incremental repair has hit diminishing returns. The 1,367 remaining joins break down as:

| Joins | Group | What blocks them |
|---|---|---|
| About 750 | Signal | Boxed in by other nets' copper, two-thirds at 198 fine-pitch parts |
| About 350 | Plane and pour nets | FIELD_GND's separate supply-return pours need the field power design; many LOGIC_GND pads have no room for a stitch via |
| 54 | Power | No room at their widths |
| 33 | Pairs | Partly blocked by placement |

The underlying cause is routing order. The current router lays one connection at a time, so early routes wall in later pads, while the inner In3 layer stays nearly empty. The standard fix is a negotiated-congestion router (the PathFinder method). It routes all connections together and repeatedly raises the cost of contested space until every connection finds its own room. It can also use In3 as a full routing layer.

I'll wait for r07's measured result, then start that build.

**Why it isn't converging.** I measured this instead of guessing. On r07's geometry I took 40 sampled failed joins and flood-filled from each source pad with different obstacle classes removed:

| Obstacles removed | Joins whose source reaches the target |
|---|---|
| nothing (as routed) | 1 / 40 |
| pours or reservation keepouts | no change (I tested my pour theory and it was wrong) |
| plane/pour stubs and stitch vias | 12 / 40 |
| plane/pour plus power traces | 17 / 40 |
| **all other nets' tracks and vias** | **32 / 40** |
| everything, including clearance margin | 38 / 40 |

The unrouted pads are caged by other nets' copper in layers: ordinary signals first, then ground and plane fan-out stubs and stitch vias behind them. The rip-up tool may only remove ordinary signals, so each round gains about 12 joins in 80 minutes. Repeating it won't finish the board, so I've held round 2. About 20 % of the remaining joins look blocked even with all routing removed; those are pad-escape and placement problems, the advisor's first item.

**What finishes it.**
1. A negotiated-congestion re-route in which signals and plane fan-outs are re-routed together, with power trunks and pours kept fixed. A new router build, verified before integration.
2. Placement and pad-escape fixes for the joins that are blocked even on an empty board. I'm generating that per-footprint list now.

E1, the fresh re-route of all ordinary signals, is routing now and will show how much simple re-ordering recovers. The low-current power step (r08) is running in the queue. This will not be finished tonight. Realistically it's a multi-session job, and the placement fixes may need decisions from you once I have the list.
